judgements.reason: no mention of slavery, servitude or the slave trade anywhere in the work/rest articles
no mention of remedies, tribunals or any enforcing body
no mention of penal offences, guilt, trials or presumption of innocence
no mention of movement, residence or State borders
no mention of marriage or consent; family appears only as beneficiary of remuneration
no mention of property or of owning anything alone or in association
no statement of the capacity in which social security is held; passage only mentions 'protection against unemployment' and 'other means of social protection'
passage lists no situations giving a right to security, so there is no second item; 'protection against unemployment' is adjacent but not an enumerated list
no mention of a social or international order or of realizing the Declaration's rights
no mention of States, groups or persons claiming rights to destroy the Declaration
no mention of arbitrary interference, privacy, home or correspondence
no mention of freedom of movement, residence or State borders
no mention of marriage or of race/nationality/religion; 'without any discrimination' is stated only about equal pay and lists no grounds
no mention of government, authority or the will of the people
no mention of motherhood, childhood or special care and assistance
no mention of duties to the community or of development of personality
no mention of torture or of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment
no mention of hearings, tribunals or equality before the law
no mention of national or international law or of penal offences
no mention of asylum, prosecutions or the United Nations
no mention of nationality or of a right to change anything; 'free choice of employment' is not framed as a right to change that may not be denied
passage grants a right to form and join trade unions but never states that no one may be compelled to belong to an association
no mention of national effort or international co-operation
no mention of special care and assistance or of motherhood and childhood
no mention of morality, public order or general welfare; the only 'limitation' is 'reasonable limitation of working hours', a different sense
no self-referential clause about interpreting the Declaration or destroying its rights
no list of items protected from arbitrary interference; 'arbitrary' does not occur
no mention of asylum, other countries or persecution
no mention of marriage or of consent of intending spouses
no mention of taking part in government, directly or through representatives
no list of security circumstances such as disability, widowhood or old age; passage mentions 'protection against unemployment' and 'social protection' only
passage never says limitations are determined by law; 'reasonable limitation of working hours' is the only limitation mentioned and no determining means is given
no mention of recognition as a person before the law or of where it applies
no mention of a hearing, of rights and obligations being determined, or of criminal charges
no mention of penalties or of penal offences
no grounds are enumerated anywhere and marriage/founding a family is not mentioned, so no count can be given
no mention of property or of deprivation, arbitrary or otherwise
no kinds of rights are enumerated as indispensable for dignity; 'dignity' appears only in 'an existence worthy of human dignity'
no mention of lack of livelihood or of circumstances beyond one's control; only 'protection against unemployment' and 'social protection' are adjacent
no mention of the community or of free and full development of personality
